summary: S/MIME actions put client part ids into IMAP FETCH unchecked
description:
# S/MIME actions put client part ids into IMAP FETCH unchecked

**Severity (our view):** Low
**CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N`

## Affected
- Component: S/MIME JSON actions
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/Tachyon/Actions/SMime.php:83` (`DoSMimeDecryptMessage`; `partId` is read at :87 and used at :101 and :107)
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/Tachyon/Actions/SMime.php:153` (`DoSMimeVerifyMessage`; `partId`/`sigPartId` are read at :156 and :171 and used at :174)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2.

## Description
Both actions build `BODY.PEEK[<partId>]` (and `[<partId>.MIME]`) from request parameters without
checking them. A value can therefore close the section bracket or the command line and append IMAP
commands of its own.

## Preconditions
An authenticated user sending requests in their own session. The CSRF token stops a cross-site
attacker.

## Impact
Limited. The commands run in the user's own IMAP session with the user's own rights, so this does
not cross accounts. It is still request input steering the IMAP protocol stream without
validation, which could matter combined with other bugs or with unusual IMAP server behaviour.

## Fix
Commit `c2706360bb1a08d85f70b5e51e44f40d20fb4614` reads both parameters through
`smimePartIdParam()`. It accepts only an IMAP section number (such as 1 or 1.2.10) or `TEXT`, and
refuses everything else, including zero or leading-zero sections and other section keywords.

## Reproduction
See `test/smime-partid.php`. It covers the new validator, so it pins the fixed behaviour rather than
reproducing the old one.

summary: SSRF gate lets through CGNAT, multicast and other ranges, and the server's own IPs
description:
# SSRF gate lets through CGNAT, multicast and other ranges, and the server's own IPs

**Severity (our view):** Low (hardens the unreleased gate from 6c485d88c)
**CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N`

## Affected
- Component: SSRF gate for outbound HTTP requests
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/tachyon_util/http/request.php:124` (`URIHasPublicHost`; the flags are at :154 and are used for literal hosts and for every resolved address)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54, since 6c485d88c (2026-09-30). The gate is in no release tag yet and does not come from SnappyMail.

## Description
`URIHasPublicHost()` relies only on `FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE | FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE`. On PHP
8.4 that still accepts 100.64.0.0/10 (shared address space: CGNAT, overlay VPNs, some cloud metadata
services), 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18.0.0/15, 224.0.0.0/4, fec0::/10 and ff00::/8. It also accepts the
server's own public addresses. A request to one of those never leaves the host, so it reaches
services that listen on every address but are firewalled from outside.

## Preconditions
An authenticated user who can make the server fetch a URL through a code path protected by this
gate.

## Impact
Requests to internal services on the webmail host, or to networks in the listed ranges that the
host can reach. How much this matters depends heavily on the deployment.

## Fix
Commit `442c28a24804550e24e2707f2ed162ea514dc37d` sends both checks (the literal host and every
resolved address) through a new `IsPublicIP()`. It applies PHP's flags, then an explicit deny list
of the ranges above, then the addresses `net_get_interfaces()` reports for this host (cached per
request). DNS rebinding between the check and the connect is still possible, as the existing code
comment already says. Closing it needs the connection pinned to the address that was checked.

## Reproduction
See `test/ssrf-ranges.php`. It fails on unpatched master, where 100.64.0.1 is treated as public.

Found by Kimi K3 (the ranges) and Claude Opus 5.5 (the server's own IPs). Verified, fixed and written up by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). Zap did not review the code; Zap started the AI review sessions and is submitting the report; see "Who did what" in the cover note.


---

**Maintainer note.** The fix as submitted was incomplete. It covered `::ffff:0:0/96` and `64:ff9b::/96` but not 6to4: `http://[2002:7f00:1::1]/` reached 127.0.0.1 and `http://[2002:a00:5::]/` reached 10.0.0.5, both returning ALLOW. 2002:V4ADDR::/48 (RFC 3056) carries the address in bytes 2 to 5. Closed in `d2655309f` with the cases added to `test/ssrf-ranges.php`. Reachability needs a configured 6to4 tunnel and RFC 7526 deprecated the mechanism, so a default host was never exposed.

summary: two-factor-auth can be disabled, replaced or read with only a session
description:
# two-factor-auth can be disabled, replaced or read with only a session

**Severity (our view):** Low-Medium
**CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N`

## Affected
- Component: `plugins/two-factor-auth`
- `plugins/two-factor-auth/index.php:159` (`DoEnableTwoFactor`, accepts disable), `:210` (`DoClearTwoFactorInfo`), `:102` (`DoCreateTwoFactorSecret`, overwrites the secret with Enable false), `:143` (`DoShowTwoFactorSecret`)
- `plugins/two-factor-auth/index.php:114` (backup codes from `rand()`)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2.

## Description
While 2-step verification is enabled, four actions need only a valid session and its CSRF token:
switching 2FA off, deleting it, replacing the secret (which also switches it off), and returning the
current secret and QR code. None of them asks for a current TOTP or backup code. Backup codes are
generated with `rand()`, which is not a cryptographically secure generator.

## Preconditions
The attacker already has the victim's session, for example a stolen session cookie or a few minutes
at an unlocked, logged-in browser.

## Impact
A session compromise can be turned into a lasting one: the second factor can be removed or copied,
so a later login with the password (obtained separately) no longer needs it. Without an existing
session there is no effect.

## Fix
Commit `4ac77a337e35c6fbfee39e76a810d15bf4d8b68b`: while 2FA is enabled, all four actions require a
current TOTP or backup code, checked the same way as at login, and a backup code used here is spent.
Enabling 2FA and the first setup are unchanged. Backup codes come from `random_int()`. The settings
page asks for the code before these actions and reloads the real state if a change is refused. The
`TwoFactorAuthSettings.min.js` that is actually served is now the same file as the source.

## Reproduction
See `test/two-factor-reauth.php`. It drives the new gate with storage and provider stubbed, so it
pins the fixed behaviour rather than reproducing the old one.

summary: Remote-image consent bypass through srcset and CSS url()
description:
# Remote-image consent bypass through srcset and CSS url()

**Severity (our view):** Medium (privacy)
**CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N`

## Affected
- Component: client-side HTML sanitizer
- `dev/Common/Html.js:285` (`sizes` and `srcset` are on the attribute allowlist and never rewritten)
- `dev/Common/Html.js:593` (only `backgroundImage`, `listStyleImage` and `content` are checked for `url()`)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2.

## Description
The sanitizer sends `img src`, and `url()` in three style properties, through the remote-content
handling: blocked until the user allows it, or rewritten to the proxy when the proxy is on. Two other
ways to load an image are left alone. One is `srcset`/`sizes`. The other is `url()` in any other
style property (for example `border-image-source`, `mask-image`, `filter`). With the proxy off, the
browser fetches these directly. With the proxy on, the CSP limits images to `'self'`. But a relative
`srcset` that points at the server's own proxy endpoint, whose URLs are unsigned, is same-origin, so
the server fetches the external URL while the message is rendered.

## Preconditions
An external sender delivers an HTML message and the recipient opens it. No click is needed. This
works with the default behaviour of asking before loading remote images.

## Impact
Read receipts and disclosure of the reader's IP address and User-Agent without the user's consent
(through the proxy, the sender instead sees the server fetch and its timing). This defeats the
remote-content blocking feature.

## Fix
Commit `7db1e9664df0ee5cecc97a94edb01bc1f2868969` removes `srcset` and `sizes` from the allowlist
(attributes not on it are deleted). It also drops any other style property whose value contains
`url()`. Relative `img src` was already safe: it is parked as `data-x-src-broken`. Signing
ProxyExternal URLs would be useful extra hardening but is not part of this commit.

## Reproduction
There is no test file. See the commit message: the style sweep was checked in Chromium. The listed
properties lose their `url()`, and other declarations survive.

summary: Raw view serves attachments inline with the sender's Content-Type
description: # Raw view serves attachments inline with the sender's Content-Type **Severity (our view):** Low **CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N` ## Affected - Component: Raw action (attachment view and download) - `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/Tachyon/Actions/Raw.php:178-183` (type taken from the message part; PDF forced only by file name) and `:216-217` (sent with `inline` disposition) - `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/Tachyon/ServiceActions.php:384` (raw CSP `script-src 'none'; child-src 'none'` replaces the global policy) - Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2. ## Description The Raw view serves an attachment inline with the Content-Type declared in the message. Take a part whose file name looks like an image but which is declared as HTML: it is previewed by its extension, and opening its link renders an HTML page on the webmail origin. The raw CSP blocks scripts. But because it replaces the global policy, it sets no `default-src`, `form-action` or `base-uri`, so forms, meta refresh, remote styles and remote images all work. `nosniff` and frame denial stay in place. ## Preconditions An external sender delivers such an attachment, and the recipient opens the attachment link. ## Impact Phishing content without scripts, such as a fake login form that posts elsewhere, shown under the real webmail hostname, which makes it convincing. There is no script execution and no direct access to session data. ## Fix Commit `4b0fd25077e16a6848bc0f1e8c3cef0d25c6f29b` adds `inlineContentType()`. Only raster images, PDF, audio, video and `text/plain` are shown as declared. Other `text/*` types are shown as `text/plain`. Everything else, SVG and XML included, is sent as an `application/octet-stream` download. The raw CSP adds `default-src 'none'`, `form-action 'none'` and `base-uri 'none'`, with explicit sources for what raw view legitimately shows. `object-src 'self'` is meant to keep the browser PDF viewer working; that was not checked in a browser. ## Reproduction See `test/raw-inline-type.php`. It covers the new type decision, so it pins the fixed behaviour rather than reproducing the old one. Found by DeepSeek V4 Flash. Verified, fixed and written up by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). Zap did not review the code; Zap started the AI review sessions and is submitting the report; see "Who did what" in the cover note. --- **Maintainer note.** Shipped behaviour differs from the fix described above. SVG is shown inline rather than downloaded, because mail legitimately uses it for logos and signatures and `linkPreview()` serves inline images through this same path. An `` never runs script, and a second `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox` header is sent alongside SVG so that opening one directly cannot run script either. Follow-up `81647c728`, released in 4.4.0. summary: ?/Test integrity diagnostic runs without login, target taken from Host
description:
# ?/Test integrity diagnostic runs without login, target taken from Host

**Severity (our view):** Medium
**CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N`

## Affected
- Component: service action `Test` (integrity diagnostic)
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/Tachyon/ServiceActions.php:579` (`ServiceTest()`, no authentication check)
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/tachyon_util/integrity.php:30` (base URL built from `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']`)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2.

## Description
`ServiceTest()` runs `Integrity::test()` for any request. The diagnostic builds its base URL from
the Host header the client sent. The server then sends HEAD requests to that URL and prints the
response status and every response header. So the requester chooses where the server sends requests
and can read the results. Behind reverse proxies that pick the virtual host by name and ignore the
port, a Host value with a different port still reaches the application.

## Preconditions
Unauthenticated network access to the instance. No configuration change is needed.

## Impact
Server-side request forgery that discloses the response status and headers. It is limited to HEAD
requests and to the diagnostic's fixed paths. It can be used to probe ports and services on the
webmail host that are not reachable from outside, and it shows deployment details to anonymous
users.

## Fix
Commit `ec5e71a37e8f20f5ddd020a7a5dc7805d345c03a` returns 404 unless an admin session is present.
An admin's browser sends the real Host, so the diagnostic still works for the people it is meant
for. Further hardening would be to stop deriving the target from `HTTP_HOST` at all.

## Reproduction
There is no test file. See the commit message: it was checked end to end with `php -S` and no
network. The unpatched code returns 200 with the diagnostics; the patched code returns 404 with no
body.

summary: avatars plugin: unauthenticated SSRF and avatar cache poisoning through BIMI and favicon lookups
description:
### Summary

The `avatars` plugin answers `GET /?Avatar/<bimi>/<base64url(email)>` without a session, takes the BIMI switch from the URL, and fetches the resulting image URL server-side with an HTTP client on which `block_private_ips` is not set. The SSRF gate added in 4.4.0 therefore does not apply here. An unauthenticated client can make the server fetch an address of its choosing, internal ones included, and can write the result into the shared avatar cache under any email address.

Only installations that enable the plugin with `bimi` (or `favicon`) on are affected; both are off by default.

### Details

Code read at kimusan/Tachyon `a2ebdfd` (4.4.0), `plugins/avatars/index.php`:

1. `ServiceAvatar()` has no session check. It decodes the email from the path and calls `getAvatar($sEmail, !empty($aBimi[0]), $sBimiSelector)`; both the BIMI flag and the selector come from the URL.
2. With `bimi` enabled, `getAvatar()` resolves `<selector>._bimi.<domain>` for the domain of that email and adds the record's `l=` URL to `$aUrls`. The domain, and therefore the URL, belong to whoever publishes the DNS record.
3. `getUrl()` creates `HTTP\Request::factory()` and calls `doRequest('GET', $sUrl)`. `canFetchURI()` only refuses private and reserved addresses when `block_private_ips` is true, and the default is false (`tachyon_util/http/request.php`). Only `ServiceProxyExternal()` sets it.
4. When the response is an image, `cacheImage($sEmail, ...)` stores it under that email, with no expiry. Later lookups for that address by logged-in users are served from the cache.
5. With `favicon` enabled, the `$bBimi` branch also calls `getFavicon($sDomain)`, which reaches the attacker's domain in the same way.

### Impact

- Unauthenticated SSRF: GET requests to loopback, private ranges, link-local and cloud metadata addresses, and to the server's own services. The body is returned only if it is an image, but the request is made, and status and timing are observable.
- Unauthenticated avatar cache poisoning: an attacker can choose the picture shown next to an arbitrary sender address (for example a company's finance mailbox) to every user of the instance.
- Usable as an anonymous request relay towards third parties.

### Suggested fix

What we deployed on our own SnappyMail 2.38.2 installation (same code path, inherited from upstream):

- require an account (`getAccountFromToken(false)`) in `ServiceAvatar()` and `DoAvatar()`;
- fetch only `https` on port 443, without following redirects, after resolving the host and checking that every address is public; pin the connection to the checked address (`CURLOPT_RESOLVE`) to close the DNS-rebinding window;
- consult the shared cache only for a message that passed DKIM, and give cache entries an expiry.

Setting `$oHTTP->block_private_ips = true` in `getUrl()` would close the SSRF part with the 4.4.0 gate; the session check is still needed for the cache poisoning. Our patch and its test (`test/avatars.php`, 23 checks) are available on request; I did not want to publish them before you had a chance to fix this.

### Reporter

Fathi Ben Nasr, Convergent Cloud Computing (found while porting your 4.4.0 fixes to our 2.38.2).

summary: Crypt tokens forgeable by picking the xxtea algorithm
description:
**Severity (our view):** Medium (defence in depth; no authentication bypass found)
**CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N`

## Affected
- Component: `Tachyon\Util\Crypt`
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/tachyon_util/crypt.php:61` (`Decrypt()` builds the method name from token field 0, at :67)
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/tachyon_util/crypt.php:264` (`XxteaDecrypt()`, key = salt followed by `Passphrase()`)
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/MailSo/Base/Xxtea.php` (uses only the first 16 bytes of the key)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2.

## Description
`Crypt::Decrypt()` takes the algorithm name from the token and calls `"{name}Decrypt"`. A client can
therefore request xxtea on any server, including servers where `Encrypt()` would never produce it.
The xxtea key is the token's own salt followed by the server passphrase. XXTEA reads only the first
16 bytes of its key, and the salt is 16 bytes, so the server secret never takes part. Anyone can
produce tokens that every `Crypt::Decrypt*` consumer accepts as genuine (remember-me, secure cookies,
`DecodeKeyValuesQ` raw keys), and anyone can decrypt existing xxtea tokens. The dispatch also accepts
any method whose name ends in `Decrypt`.

## Preconditions
Unauthenticated network access to the instance.

## Impact
The integrity guarantee these consumers rely on does not hold. We traced every consumer we found.
Each one still requires a server-side record (remember-me needs a stored random token) or a real
IMAP login, so we found no account takeover. Code that trusts `Crypt::Decrypt*` output on its own,
now or in plugins, would be exposed. On hosts without sodium and openssl, real xxtea tokens also
lose their confidentiality.

## Fix
Commit `507c614a5d64ec0bb072ccc2915c0e73f9205df3` makes `Decrypt` refuse xxtea whenever sodium or
openssl is available, compare the algorithm name case-insensitively, and dispatch only to sodium,
openssl and xxtea. The xxtea key becomes the first 16 bytes of `sha256(salt . passphrase)`, so on a
host that has only xxtea the key depends on the secret. Tokens written under the old derivation stop
decrypting on such hosts.

## Reproduction
See `test/crypt-forgery.php`. It needs the sodium and openssl extensions and fails on unpatched
master.

Found by GPT-6 Astra Pro. Verified, fixed and written up by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). Zap did not review the code; Zap started the AI review sessions and is submitting the report; see "Who did what" in the cover note.

summary: S/MIME verify reports altered messages as validly signed
description:
**Severity (our view):** Medium
**CVSS 3.1 suggestion:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`

## Affected
- Component: S/MIME signature verification
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/tachyon_util/smime/openssl.php:289` (`verify()`; the flags are at :303, and the function returns `'success' => true` whenever the call succeeds)
- The result is passed on by `Tachyon/Actions/SMime.php` and displayed by the client (`Message.js`, `smimeSigned`)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2.

## Description
`OpenSSL::verify()` calls `openssl_pkcs7_verify` with `PKCS7_NOVERIFY | PKCS7_NOCHAIN | PKCS7_NOSIGS`.
`PKCS7_NOSIGS` tells OpenSSL not to check the signature, so the call succeeds for any well-formed
signed message, and the function then reports `success: true`. The client displays that as a good
signature. This affects the message view, the explicit verify action and signed content inside
decrypted mail.

## Preconditions
Anyone who can send mail to a Tachyon user can send a signed message whose content was changed
after signing. The recipient only has to open it.

## Impact
The signature indicator can be forged: altered or invalidly signed content is shown as signed by the
certificate holder. Users who rely on S/MIME to judge whether a message is authentic (for example
payment instructions or key changes) can be misled. There is no confidentiality impact.

## Fix
Commit `cc66b54873396e434a2c37a458a946480c8245cb` keeps the existing call, which is also how the
content of opaque signed messages is extracted. It adds a second `openssl_pkcs7_verify` call without
`PKCS7_NOSIGS`; that call decides `success` and does not throw on failure. A message with a broken
signature stays readable but is no longer reported as signed. `PKCS7_NOVERIFY` is kept on purpose,
and a comment now explains it: success means the content is what the certificate holder signed, not
that the certificate is trusted by a CA. You may want to report chain trust as a separate field
later.

## Reproduction
See `test/smime-verify.php`. It needs the openssl extension and fails on unpatched master.

Found by GPT-6 Astra Pro. Verified, fixed and written up by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic). Zap did not review the code; Zap started the AI review sessions and is submitting the report; see "Who did what" in the cover note.

summary: Header injection into replies through an encoded-word Message-ID
description:
Hi Kim,

I'm Zap and I have created a fresh downstream fork of Tachyon today,
github.com/ZaphodB/Tachyon, which I'm moving my webmail to. Before switching I
started AI models on security reviews of Tachyon master (c988e3a54). They turned
up nine issues, which I'm filing as separate private advisories, as your
SECURITY.md asks.

To be clear about who did what: **I did not review the code**, and I have not
reviewed the fixes either. I started the AI review sessions, agreed to have the
findings fixed, and decided to report them to you. Everything else (finding the
issues, verifying them, writing the fixes and tests, and writing these reports)
was done by AI models. The details are in "Who did what" below.

**First, something I need to own up to.** On 2026-10-06 at about 20:12 UTC
(22:12 CEST) the branch with the fixes was pushed to my **public** fork, before
anyone had told you:

https://github.com/ZaphodB/Tachyon/tree/security/review-2026-10-06

The AI agent working for me pushed it after I said go, and neither of us stopped
to see that this disclosed the issues. The commits say plainly what each fix
closes, and the diffs show the rest, so please treat all nine as **publicly
visible since that time**. I'm sorry. It takes away your chance to fix them
before disclosure and shortens your timeline. I'm leaving the branch up, because
taking it down now would not un-disclose anything (GitHub keeps fork commits
reachable through the parent repository anyway), but if you would rather I
delete it, say so and I will.

## Reports

| # | Advisory | Severity (our view) | Found by | Fix commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | Header injection into replies through an encoded-word Message-ID | Medium (more impact if PHP `mail()` is the transport) | DeepSeek V4 Flash | 1248b0522 |
| 02 | S/MIME verify reports altered messages as validly signed | Medium | GPT-6 Astra Pro | cc66b5487 |
| 03 | Crypt tokens forgeable by picking the xxtea algorithm | Medium (no auth bypass found) | GPT-6 Astra Pro | 507c614a5 |
| 04 | `?/Test` integrity diagnostic runs without login, target taken from `Host` | Medium | DeepSeek V4 Flash, GPT-6 Astra Pro | ec5e71a37 |
| 05 | Raw view serves attachments inline with the sender's Content-Type | Low | DeepSeek V4 Flash | 4b0fd2507 |

## Affected
- Component: MIME header parsing (MailSo) and outgoing message headers
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/MailSo/Base/Utils.php:211` (`DecodeHeaderValue`; CR/LF are replaced at :221, before encoded-words are decoded)
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/MailSo/Mime/Message.php:175` (`SetInReplyTo` only trims); `:168` (`SetSubject`, no check)
- `tachyon/v/0.0.0/app/libraries/MailSo/Mime/Header.php:32` (no line-break check on outgoing values)
- Versions: Tachyon master c988e3a54 and earlier. Inherited from SnappyMail; the same code is in v2.38.2.

## Description
`DecodeHeaderValue` replaces CR, LF and tab before it decodes RFC 2047 encoded-words, so an
encoded-word whose decoded text contains a line break comes out with the break intact. When the
user replies or forwards, the client copies the original message's Message-ID into In-Reply-To,
and `SetInReplyTo` passes it on after a `trim()`. `Header` does not reject line breaks either, so
the decoded value becomes extra header lines in the outgoing message, or the start of a body if it
contains an empty line. Subject on "Edit as new" has the same shape. We checked References and the
normal reply/forward Subject, and they are not affected.

## Preconditions
Any external sender can deliver such a message. It takes effect when the recipient replies to it or
forwards it from Tachyon. No other interaction or configuration is needed.

## Impact
The reply is sent from the user's account with headers or body text chosen by the original sender.
Where signing is set up, it is DKIM-signed by the user's domain, and it is stored in Sent. With SMTP
as the transport, an injected Bcc header adds no recipient because the envelope is built separately,
so recipients see forged headers or body text but nobody new receives the mail. With PHP `mail()` as
the transport, an injected recipient header does add a recipient, so the reply can be copied to a
third party.

## Fix
Commit `1248b0522f06d43631f6a1f9eab358bd2776975d` strips CR, LF and NUL in two places: after
decoding in `DecodeHeaderValue`, and in `Header` itself. Every outgoing header is built through
`Header`, so values that arrive by other routes (client parameters, plugins) cannot break the line
either. Header folding is unaffected because `__toString` adds it back.

## Reproduction
See `test/header-injection.php`. It fails on unpatched master.
